## Historical audit — H0190

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane4/codex_parallel_12_lane4_B_r2/infer_logs/obsidian-linter-auto-table-of-contents/turn_1/trajs.json`. Event references below are to this file’s `main_agent` trace. The inventory metadata supplies the reported patch and evaluation figures; the underlying evaluation file was not separately observed.

| Aspect | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The inferred goal was to add an automatic table-of-contents rule to Obsidian Linter. The original task request is not shown, so detailed behavior cannot be reconstructed. The student planned implementation and verification on a branch from `main` (event 1). |
| Autonomous exploration | The student inspected repository state, rule conventions, registration, ignore handling, Markdown parsing, localization, and an existing test harness (events 2–13, 15–17, 19–30). This is exploration, not an implementation. |
| Actual change | Git initially showed detached HEAD and `master` (event 5). The student created `auto-toc` from `master`; Git confirmed the switch (events 14, 18). Inventory reports a zero-byte patch. No source edit or commit appears in the supplied trace; the student explicitly reported the implementation and requested commit incomplete (event 33). |
| Visible validation | A Node assertion checked whether `src/rules/auto-toc.ts` existed and failed with “AutoToc rule is missing” (events 31–32). This establishes absence of that file at the check, not a behavioral test of a TOC algorithm. No build or student-run test suite is visible. |
| Formal outcome | Inventory labels the result `empty_patch_formally_not_solved`, with 0/41 fail-to-pass and 1131/1131 pass-to-pass. Those are reported evaluation figures, not evidence of partial implementation. The session ended normally with `end_turn`; no technical interruption is established (top-level metadata). |
| Teacher input | Shared hint paths are listed as available, but neither captured system-prompt text nor a delivered teacher event is included in the observations. Receipt and adoption are therefore unestablished; exploration alone cannot prove either. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, inspecting conventions and reproducing an absent artifact can orient work, but neither substitutes for an implementation and its validation. Task-specific observations are the available `master` base and missing `auto-toc.ts` file. Why the student stopped after exploration remains unknown; the record does not establish an algorithm failure or its cause. This is a coding trace, not a Scene task, so visual and geometric checks are not applicable.
